newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mondi's Swazi operation hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: Mondi's Swazi operation hit by strike.

text.p: South African paper and timber producer Mondi Ltd said a strike by about 85 percent of its workforce at its Swaziland Peak Timber sawmill went into a third day on Wednesday.

The strike had began on Monday in response to a call by the Swaziland Federation of Trade Unions (SFTU) for two days of mass protests to push forward demands for democratic reforms in the landlocked mountain kingdom.
Mondi spokeswoman Monique Fernandes declined to say how much the company was losing through the action by members of the SFTU's affiliate, the Swaziland Agricultural and Plantation Workers Union.
"The strike at our sawmill in Swaziland is continuing. There is only 15 percent of the workforce carrying out essential services at the mill," she told Reuters.
The Peak Timber sawmill near Piggs Peak in Swaziland employs about 421 people, she said, adding the company saw no immediate end to the strike.
Mondi is a unit of Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd (Amic).

SFTU officials vowed on Tuesday that the mass stayaways and protests, which have also affected Swaziland's sugar industry -- the country's largest foreign exchange earner -- would continue indefinitely.
The Swaziland Sugar Association has estimated its losses at about three million rand a day.
